final_answer:
The **sunk cost fallacy** occurs when people continue investing time, money, or effort into a decision simply because they have already invested in it, even if it is no longer rational to do so. Here are three real-world examples from different domains:

1. **Business**: A company continues to fund a failing product line because it has already spent millions on development, even though it would be more logical to cut losses and pivot to a new idea.

2. **Personal Life**: A person remains in an unhappy relationship because they have spent years and emotional energy on it, even though the relationship is no longer healthy or fulfilling.

3. **Education**: A student persists in a difficult course even when they are not learning anything meaningful, simply because they have already invested time and effort into it.
